title: The can/tin is placed in a place where the character on the original video puts his foot over and it makes him seem like stepping on the can, which doesn't happen in real life physics and logic because the no one steps on a can/tin.

Camera: static, vertical, medium-wide, the same framing in all three frames. …

In the second and third frames the can is mostly hidden, so its position relative to the feet there cannot be read clearly. frames_seen.seen: Gym scene, vertical framing, camera static at the same spot in all three frames. The man is at the left edge, walking toward the rack with his body turned left. He wears a dark sleeveless top, dark loose trousers and grey sneakers with white stripes. The Celsius can stands upright on the grey rubber floor in front of the lower dumbbell shelf, at about the height of his shin. …

The man is in the middle of the frame, bent forward at the waist with both hands reaching toward the dumbbells on the middle shelf. His legs are apart and his rear foot is raised off the floor. The can stands on the floor just behind his legs, partly hidden by his trousers, near his shoe. Only its upper body and label show.

The man is at the right side of the frame, bent further forward with both hands on a dumbbell on the lower shelf. His trousers and shoes are close to the floor. The can is mostly hidden behind his leg near the rack base, with only a small red and white fragment visible.
